ety.text: Per Vasmer from во́лух (vólux), from вол (vol, “ox”), i.e. initially воло́вий пасту́х (volóvij pastúx, “ox shepherd”). Dismissed by Chernykh. Per Chernykh akin to волхв (volxv) (note о́лух царя́ небе́сного (ólux carjá nebésnovo)). Alternatively from Old East Slavic *оглухъ (*ogluxŭ), whence Ukrainian оглух (ohlux, “someone hard of hearing”), due to association between глухова́тый (gluxovátyj, “hard of hearing”) and глу́пый (glúpyj, “stupid”). Attested since 1769.
